verdicts.title: Unpolyfilled Array/String .at(-1) crashes on Safari < 15.4 while build target floor is safari14
verdicts.reason: Confirmed: vite.config.ts sets no build.target, so Vite/esbuild use the default 'modules' preset (baseline includes safari14), and esbuild only down-levels syntax, not runtime methods like Array.prototype.at/String.prototype.at. wikilinks.ts:146 calls `.at(-1)` directly on the hot wikilink-label render path with no guard/polyfill. Array.prototype.at shipped in Safari 15.4 (Mar 2022), so on Safari/iOS 14.x-15.3 this throws TypeError and breaks wikilink rendering — a genuine gap between the declared build floor and the API actually used.

verdicts.title: Search dialog input relies on React autoFocus; iOS WebKit will not raise the soft keyboard
verdicts.reason: The dialog is opened either via a button's onClick (App.tsx onOpenSearch) or a window keydown listener, both discrete user-gesture events. React 18 flushes updates from discrete events (click, keydown) synchronously before the handler returns rather than deferring to a later microtask/macrotask, so the autoFocus-driven .focus() call in SearchDialog.tsx:159 commits within the same synchronous gesture-handling stack, not 'a microtask after the click ends' as claimed. The finding's premise about React's commit timing is inaccurate, and in practice React modals with autoFocus reliably raise the iOS keyboard when triggered by a tap. This is a speculative/uncorroborated claim, not a demonstrated defect in the cited code.
